title: RailOne App Reaches 4.76 Crore Downloads, Records 10 Lakh Daily Average Ticket Bookings
subtitle:
RailOne App Integrates Reserved, Unreserved & Platform Ticketing, Train & PNR Enquiry, RailMadad and Other Key Railway Services on a Single Platform
NTES Handles Over 6 Crore Daily Enquiries and 80,000 Concurrent Users, Reducing Queues & Waiting Time at Railway Enquiry Counters
body_text:
With a view to expand digital mode of procurement of reserved as well as unreserved tickets Railways has launched RailOne App on 01.07.2025. This App enables passengers to book reserved as well as unreserved tickets on mobile phone. This App combines all the public facing services of Indian Railways like reserved ticketing, unreserved ticketing and platform ticketing, train enquiry, PNR enquiry, Railmadad, etc. into a single platform. This, in effect, brings the Passenger reservation system facility to passenger's palm.  The App facilitates users to access multiple services through Single-Sign-On (SSO) facility eliminating the necessity of downloading multiple Applications of Railways & remembering several passwords.
The details of transactions through Railone app as on 02.08.2026 are as under: -
Daily Average tickets 10 lakhs Reserved tickets 2.79 lakhs Unreserved tickets 7.24 lakhs Downloads 4.76 crores
The National Train Enquiry System (NTES), implemented in the year 2000, provides passengers with near real-time train running information, including arrival/departure status and train schedules through multiple interfaces such as enquiry counters, the NTES website, mobile applications (Android & iOS) and the nationwide Rail Enquiry Number 139. Its key features include Spot Your Train, Live Station, Train Schedule, and Trains between Stations, enabling passengers to access authentic and reliable information conveniently. The NTES mobile application, launched in October 2014 (Android) and October 2015 (iOS), has recorded more than 4.5 crore downloads on Android and 16 lakh downloads on iOS as on 01.08.2026. At present, NTES handles about 80,000 concurrent users and processes over 6 crore enquiries daily. It has been generally appreciated by the passengers.
The deployment of the National Train Enquiry System (NTES), which provides passengers with easy access to authentic and near real-time train running information through multiple digital platforms including the website, mobile applications and Rail Enquiry Number 139, has significantly reduced the need for passengers to visit railway enquiry counters. Consequently, this has helped in reducing queues and waiting time at enquiry counters.
In cases of train cancellation, the online e-ticketing system NGeT(Next Generation E-ticketing) automatically initiates the process of refund immediately after the scheduled time of departure of the train and the applicable refund is credited to the passenger's bank account. Automatic refunds linked to train cancellation are presently available only for e-Tickets booked online and are not available for counter tickets in which case the passenger holding counter ticket is required to visit nearest PRS counter.
RailOne is the Official App of Indian Railways which provides integrated platform for all public facing services of IR. It offers reserved, unreserved and platform ticketing, journey plan, train information, passenger support and allied railway services through a single, seamless mobile application.
Presently approximately 89% of the reserved tickets are booked online as compared to about 49% in 2013-14. Unreserved tickets booked through various non-counter modes has increased to nearly 39%.
This information was provided by the Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, in a reply to a question in the Lok Sabha today.
*****
Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Vanshita Jaiswal

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Railways informed the Lok Sabha that the RailOne App, launched on 01.07.2025 to integrate reserved, unreserved and platform ticketing along with train enquiry, PNR status and RailMadad, has crossed 4.76 crore downloads and now averages 10 lakh ticket bookings daily (2.79 lakh reserved and 7.24 lakh unreserved) as of 02.08.2026. The release also highlighted the National Train Enquiry System (NTES), which handles over 6 crore enquiries daily and up to 80,000 concurrent users, reducing crowding at railway enquiry counters. Currently about 89% of reserved tickets are booked online (up from 49% in 2013-14), and nearly 39% of unreserved tickets are booked via non-counter modes.
enrichment.context:
Indian Railways has been steadily digitizing passenger services to reduce counter dependency, improve transparency, and enhance user convenience, in line with the broader Digital India push. RailOne consolidates previously fragmented apps (like UTS for unreserved tickets, IRCTC Rail Connect for reserved tickets, and NTES for train enquiry) into a single Single-Sign-On platform, simplifying the digital ecosystem for over a billion annual rail passengers. This follows a global and domestic trend of super-app consolidation in public service delivery, aimed at improving ease of living and reducing transaction costs for citizens.

The NTES, operational since 2000, has been a backbone of passenger information services, and its digital penetration (mobile app downloads exceeding 4.6 crore combined) reflects the shift away from physical enquiry counters toward self-service digital channels. This has downstream implications for railway station infrastructure planning, staffing at enquiry counters, and overall efficiency gains. The mention of the NGeT (Next Generation e-Ticketing) system's automatic refund mechanism for cancelled trains also underscores incremental improvements in passenger grievance redress and financial ease, though a digital divide persists since counter-ticket holders still need to visit PRS counters for refunds, highlighting continued reliance on physical infrastructure for less digitally-enabled passengers.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the RailOne App launched by Indian Railways:
1. It integrates reserved, unreserved, and platform ticketing along with train enquiry and PNR status services.
2. It was launched on 1st July 2025.
3. It replaced the National Train Enquiry System (NTES) entirely.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: RailOne integrates reserved, unreserved, and platform ticketing along with enquiry services and was launched on 01.07.2025, but it did not replace NTES, which continues to operate as a separate real-time train information system handling over 6 crore daily enquiries.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to Indian Railways' digital initiatives, which of the following statements is correct?
options: NGeT provides automatic refunds for both e-tickets and counter tickets upon train cancellation.
NGeT provides automatic refunds only for e-tickets booked online upon train cancellation.
NTES was launched in 2025 alongside RailOne.
Approximately 49% of reserved tickets are currently booked online.
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, automatic refunds through the Next Generation e-Ticketing (NGeT) system are available only for online e-tickets; counter ticket holders must visit PRS counters. NTES was implemented in 2000, and currently about 89% (not 49%) of reserved tickets are booked online.
